name: Coriky
label: Dischord
lede: Half of Fugazi and half of the Evens, three years of practicing before anyone heard a note, a first show billed as an open practice in a church, and a debut that had to wait out a pandemic.

eras.title: Home from Rome
eras.text: Joe Lally had spent years living in Rome with his family, making solo records after Fugazi stopped. When he moved back to Washington in 2015, he started playing with Ian MacKaye and Amy Farina of The Evens, and a duo quietly turned into a trio.

years.h: Joe Lally comes home and joins Ian MacKaye and Amy Farina
years.p: [[Joe Lally|62046ffd-7d76-476b-bee5-b281b7575c6c]] returns to D.C. and starts playing with Ian MacKaye and Amy Farina of The Evens. It's the first band MacKaye and Lally have shared since Fugazi's hiatus, with MacKaye on regular guitar and Farina on drums.
years.xp:
Lally and MacKaye founded Fugazi together in 1987, and Lally played bass there until the band's indefinite hiatus. In the years between he ran the Tolotta label through Dischord, played with [[John Frusciante|f1571db1-c672-4a54-a2cf-aaa329f26f0b]] in [[Ataxia|c2b5da4f-31c2-4a02-80a1-e00008378157]], and made three solo albums while living in Italy.

Dischord's bio for Coriky is short and a little wry: established in 2015, and no first show until 2018.

eras.title: An open practice in a church
eras.text: Three years in, MacKaye, Farina and Lally still had no public band name and no record. Its first appearance came the way so much D.C. punk has: a benefit, in a church, with the money going somewhere that mattered.

years.h: MacKaye, Farina and Lally's first show: a Loaves & Fishes benefit
years.p: Ian MacKaye, Amy Farina and Joe Lally, still unnamed, play St. Stephen's church in Washington, billed not as a concert but as an open practice, to raise money for the Loaves & Fishes meal program. MacKaye asks the crowd not to film.
years.xp: Brooklyn Vegan pieced the night together from fan photos and posts. One attendee called it a bit rough, with good vibes, and summed up the sound as the Evens with a Fugazi groove.

eras.title: A debut that waited out the lockdown
eras.text: Coriky made its debut album the old Dischord way, with Don Zientara at Inner Ear. Then the world shut down two weeks before release day, and the band chose the record stores over the calendar.

years.h: Coriky records its debut at Inner Ear with Don Zientara
years.p: Coriky's album is recorded at Inner Ear with Don Zientara, the engineer behind decades of Dischord records, with MacKaye, Farina and Lally doing extra engineering and mixing themselves.

years.h: The trio goes public as Coriky and shares Clean Kill
years.p: Ian MacKaye, Amy Farina and Joe Lally announce the band as Coriky, after Kuriki, a dice game Wikipedia calls popular with touring bands. They set a March 27 date for the debut album and share Clean Kill.

years.h: Coriky plays a free preview show in a D.C. church
years.p: Coriky play a free show at St. Stephen and the Incarnation Episcopal Church in Washington, a few weeks before their debut album is due.

q: As close to the much-missed Fugazi as it gets in 2020.
years.h: Coriky comes out, held back for shuttered record shops
years.p: Coriky's debut was set for March 27, 2020, until COVID-19 lockdowns closed record stores. Dischord No. 190 came out digitally June 12 and on pink vinyl and CD June 26.
years.xp:
Rather than drop the album online while the stores that sell Dischord records were dark, the band and label pushed it back. Too Many Husbands followed as a second single in May.

Eleven songs in 37 minutes, from Clean Kill to Woulda Coulda. Metacritic scored it 84, Pitchfork gave it 7.8, and Stereogum made it album of the week.

Kitty Empire gave it four stars in the Guardian and made the comparison everyone was waiting to make.

years.p: Mojo puts Coriky at No. 32 of its 75 best albums of 2020, and Metacritic ranks it fifth among the year's best debuts.

sources.title: Brooklyn Vegan: Ian MacKaye, Joe Lally & Amy Farina's band played their first show
